[MUQATIL:25:44/r1] MUQATIL, d. 150 · author | holds | Most do not hear or understand guidance and resemble cattle absorbed in eating and drinking without regard for the afterlife.
[MUQATIL:25:44/r2] MUQATIL, d. 150 · author | holds | They are more astray than cattle, which recognize and remember their Lord, whereas the Meccan unbelievers do not know Him to affirm His oneness.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمنإمالةالألفيميلهافيهناسمنالعربكثير)#716/r1] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | A following enclitic hā may be transparent: a nearby kasra pulls the preceding alif toward imāla, as though the hā were absent.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمنإمالةالألفيميلهافيهناسمنالعربكثير)#716/r10] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | Arab imāla systems differ: one speaker may imāle forms another leaves open, and this variation is not defective mixing.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمنإمالةالألفيميلهافيهناسمنالعربكثير)#716/r11] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | Speakers whose dialect avoids imāla in the earlier categories avoid it throughout this category too.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمنإمالةالألفيميلهافيهناسمنالعربكثير)#716/r12] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | Imāla spreads leftward: when an alif is imāled, the preceding material is imāled too, including the material before a hā treated as absent.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمنإمالةالألفيميلهافيهناسمنالعربكثير)#716/r13] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | Some who imāle يدا leave يدها un-imāled because fatha dominates and the yāʾ before dāl is not treated like a weak alif.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمنإمالةالألفيميلهافيهناسمنالعربكثير)#716/r14] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | Most of the stronger imāla group leave رمى un-imāled, avoiding a movement toward yāʾ; unlike حبلى and معزى, its alif is not a substitute for yāʾ.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمنإمالةالألفيميلهافيهناسمنالعربكثير)#716/r15] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | Some imāle the hā-pronoun forms only at pause; in connected speech they restore alif because it is clearer, though others retain imāla in connection.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمنإمالةالألفيميلهافيهناسمنالعربكثير)#716/r16] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | reports | Some Arabs occasionally imāle forms with no regular trigger, treating word-final alif like the alif in حبلى; Sībawayh says this is rare.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمنإمالةالألفيميلهافيهناسمنالعربكثير)#716/r17] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | Some speakers leave عبدا and عنبا open when strong consonants separate the kasra from alif; imāla in عمادا and معزانا is analogical where kasra is stronger.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمنإمالةالألفيميلهافيهناسمنالعربكثير)#716/r18] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | A kasra that is more firmly present gives a stronger basis for imāla.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمنإمالةالألفيميلهافيهناسمنالعربكثير)#716/r2] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | The closer the kasra is to the alif, the stronger the case for imāla; a hā between them does not prevent it.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمنإمالةالألفيميلهافيهناسمنالعربكثير)#716/r3] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | Speakers also imāle alif near yāʾ, as in بيني وبينها; yāʾ can motivate the shift just as kasra does.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمنإمالةالألفيميلهافيهناسمنالعربكثير)#716/r4] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | A ḍamma between alif and kasra blocks imāla in raised forms such as يكيلها, unlike the accusative environment.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمنإمالةالألفيميلهافيهناسمنالعربكثير)#716/r5] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | Without a nearby yāʾ or kasra, forms such as يعلمها and يخفها do not attract imāla.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمنإمالةالألفيميلهافيهناسمنالعربكثير)#716/r6] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | A nearby yāʾ triggers imāla in forms such as فينا and علينا; speakers likewise use it in رأيت يدا and بيني وبينها.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمنإمالةالألفيميلهافيهناسمنالعربكثير)#716/r7] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | Alif in دما and دمها is not imāled because neither a kasra nor a yāʾ provides the trigger.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمنإمالةالألفيميلهافيهناسمنالعربكثير)#716/r8] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | The hā in عندها does not block imāla because عند itself would be imāled; the hā is treated as absent.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمنإمالةالألفيميلهافيهناسمنالعربكثير)#716/r9] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · بنو تميم | reports | Banu Tamim, and also some Qays and Asad speakers, use forms such as رأيت عدا and هو منا; Sībawayh treats these as dialectal patterns.
[SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكترباوجندلاوماأشبههذا|فإنأدخلتلكفقلتتربالكفإن#123/r1] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | Accusative curses such as تربا وجندلا omit a verb; the expression means may God afflict you with dust and stones, and substitutes for تربت يداك and جندلت.
[SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكترباوجندلاوماأشبههذا|فإنأدخلتلكفقلتتربالكفإن#123/r2] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | reports | Some Arabs raise ترب and جندل as a subject with a following predicate; the poetic line preserves the same curse meaning as the accusative construction.
[SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكترباوجندلاوماأشبههذا|فإنأدخلتلكفقلتتربالكفإن#123/r3] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | The formula فاها لفيك means a calamity or disaster for you; its wording replaces the verbal phrase دهاك الله, with the verb understood.
[SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكترباوجندلاوماأشبههذا|فإنأدخلتلكفقلتتربالكفإن#123/r4] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · أبو سدرة الهجمي | reports | Abū Sidrah al-Hujaymī supplies poetry illustrating the formula فاها لفيك; Sībawayh says a trusted source transmitted the lines.
[SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكترباوجندلاوماأشبههذا|فإنأدخلتلكفقلتتربالكفإن#123/r5] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | A line by ʿĀmir ibn al-Aḥwaṣ describes a calamity as having a mouth, confirming the sense of فاها as a disaster formula.
[YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p483#2/r1] YAHYA-SALLAM, d. 200 · author | holds | The people who think the majority of the polytheists hear or reason are referring to that group; they are like the livestock involved in their worship and even further astray.
[TAB-FULL:v17p459#2/r1] TAB-FULL, d. 310 · author | holds | A pagan who takes desire as god worships whichever idol he chooses; if he sees a better stone, he abandons the first and worships the new one.
[TAB-FULL:v17p459#2/r2] TAB-FULL, d. 310 · author | holds | Muhammad is not a guardian over such a person’s acts, given the person’s great ignorance.
[TAB-FULL:v17p459#2/r3] TAB-FULL, d. 310 · author | holds | The pagans do not hear the recitation in a way that lets them understand it or grasp God's proofs.

[ZAJJAJ:v4p69/r5] ZAJJAJ, d. 311 · author | holds | They resemble cattle in lacking discernment about the signs and proofs presented to them.

[IBNABIHATIM:v8p2700/r1] IBNABIHATIM, d. 327 · ابن عباس | reports | Ibn ʿAbbās says the disbelievers neither hear nor see guidance nor comprehend it.

[IBNABIHATIM:v8p2700/r3] IBNABIHATIM, d. 327 · ابن عباس | reports | Ibn ʿAbbās compares disbelievers to livestock: they hear a voice but do not understand an admonition to do good or avoid evil.

[NAHHAS:v3p161/r13] NAHHAS, d. 338 · author | holds | The wording avoids saying they will not believe because some of them were known to believe.
[NAHHAS:v3p161/r14] NAHHAS, d. 338 · author | holds | ‘Do they hear?’ means hear with acceptance, and ‘reason’ means reflect on the Prophet’s words and understand them; otherwise they are like those who neither hear nor reason.
[NAHHAS:v3p161/r15] NAHHAS, d. 338 · author | reports | Another explanation is that they gain no benefit from what they hear, so it is as though they had not heard.

[RAZI-FULL:v24p75/r8] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | holds | The disconnected “am” means “rather”; it shifts to a harsher rebuke because their stubbornness keeps them from listening or reflecting, so they are likened to animals that do not benefit from speech or thought.

[IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p113#2/r3] IBNKATHIR-FULL, d. 774 · author | holds | Most rejecters neither truly hear nor reason and are worse off than grazing livestock: animals fulfill their purpose, while humans were made to worship God alone yet associate partners despite proof and messengers.

[BIQAI-FULL:v5p321/r6] BIQAI-FULL, d. 885 · author | holds | They resemble cattle in failing to use reason and are even more astray: unlike cattle, they do not heed warnings, thank benefactors, avoid enemies, desire reward, or fear punishment.
[BIQAI-FULL:v5p321/r7] BIQAI-FULL, d. 885 · author | holds | Their misguidance veils reason; if they believed, the veils would lift and faith would illuminate their sight of subtle meanings and hidden realities.
[BIQAI-FULL:v5p322/r1] BIQAI-FULL, d. 885 · author | holds | Just as physical sight cannot distinguish visible things without sunlight, the intellect's spiritual insight cannot grasp meanings as they are without faith's light; spiritual insight is the soul's eye, as sight is the body's. | mentions 10:9
[BIQAI-FULL:v5p322/r2] BIQAI-FULL, d. 885 · author | holds | God's work in the inward realm illuminates it with the sun of spiritual knowledge just as He works in the outward world, showing how He deprives them of benefit from what He gave them.
[DURR-FULL:v6p260/r7] DURR-FULL, d. 911 · ابن عباس | reports | Ibn ʿAbbās compares disbelievers to livestock: they hear a command or admonition only as sound and do not understand its meaning.
[DURR-FULL:v6p260/r8] DURR-FULL, d. 911 · مقاتل | reports | Muqātil explains 'more astray in the path' to mean that they have missed the way.
[BURSEVI:v6p158#2/r1] BURSEVI, d. 1127 · author | holds | Livestock follow whoever guides them, recognize benefactors, seek what helps, and avoid what harms; these people neither submit to their Lord nor distinguish His beneficence from Satan’s harm, seek reward, or avoid punishment.
[BURSEVI:v6p158#2/r2] BURSEVI, d. 1127 · author | holds | Animals hold no beliefs and acquire no good or evil, whereas these people do; human ignorance also provokes strife and turns others from the truth.
[BURSEVI:v6p158#2/r3] BURSEVI, d. 1127 · author | holds | Animals cannot seek perfection and so are not negligent or blameworthy, whereas people can and are culpable for neglect deserving severe punishment.
[BURSEVI:v6p158#2/r4] BURSEVI, d. 1127 · author | holds | God created angels with reason, beasts with appetite, and humans with both; when appetite overcomes reason a person is worse than beasts, while reason overcoming appetite makes a person like the angels.
[BURSEVI:v6p158#2/r5] BURSEVI, d. 1127 · author | holds | A person who masters his own desires is better than the angels, as the verse about the best of creation states. | mentions 98:7
[BURSEVI:v6p158#2/r6] BURSEVI, d. 1127 · المثنوي | reports | The Mathnawi depicts angels as reason and worship without appetite, beasts as appetite without knowledge, and humans as divided between an upward and downward pull.
[BURSEVI:v6p158/r1] BURSEVI, d. 1127 · بعض المفسرين | reports | Some commentators hold that this verse was abrogated by the sword verse.
[BURSEVI:v6p158/r2] BURSEVI, d. 1127 · author | holds | “Do you suppose” means “rather, do you think”; true hearing is hearing the recited signs, while understanding means grasping their admonitions and calls to virtue.
[BURSEVI:v6p158/r3] BURSEVI, d. 1127 · author | holds | “Most” is specified because some did believe or recognize the truth but resisted it to protect their leadership.
[BURSEVI:v6p158/r4] BURSEVI, d. 1127 · ابن عطاء | reports | Ibn ʿAṭāʾ says a caller’s words reach people only if they heard the primordial call; their response to the prophet is a blessing of that pre-eternal response, while heedlessness reflects their distance from its source.
[BURSEVI:v6p158/r5] BURSEVI, d. 1127 · author | holds | They resemble livestock because they gain no benefit from revealed warnings or observed proofs, remaining heedless and misguided.
[BURSEVI:v6p158/r6] BURSEVI, d. 1127 · التأويلات النجمية | reports | The Najmī Interpretations says their only appetite is food, drink, and satisfying the ego’s desires, like livestock.
[ALUSI-FULL:v19p24#2/r1] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · author | holds | أم shifts from the preceding objection and denies that the Prophet should think most of them can truly hear or reason, despite his earnest preaching and guidance.
[ALUSI-FULL:v19p24#2/r2] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · author | prefers | The preferred reading asks whether they truly hear the Qur'anic verses or understand the signs in the world and themselves, so that the Prophet should invest hope and care in their faith; hearing comes first because it better suits the context.
[ALUSI-FULL:v19p24#2/r3] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · author | reports | Another reading asks whether they hear the recited verses or understand the admonitions within them that deter vice and call to virtue, explaining the Prophet's effort to guide them.
[ALUSI-FULL:v19p24#2/r4] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · author | holds | The pronouns refer to 'who' by its meaning for most of them and by its grammatical form for 'upon them'; plural suits the word 'most,' while an earlier singular treats their shared desire as one.
[ALUSI-FULL:v19p24#2/r5] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · author | rejects | The claim that 'most of them' means the unbelievers rather than the antecedent 'who' is rejected because the singular عليه rules it out.
[ALUSI-FULL:v19p24#2/r6] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · author | holds | Only most are specified because some later received the prior gift of faith and some heard or understood but resisted from arrogance or fear of losing leadership.
[ALUSI-FULL:v19p24#2/r7] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · author | holds | The comparison to cattle begins a new sentence that renews the rebuke, closes off the mistaken hope, and says they fail to benefit from warning verses or contemplate clear signs.
[ALUSI-FULL:v19p25/r1] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · author | holds | Cattle obey their caretaker, recognize kindness and harm, seek benefit, avoid danger, and find food, water, and shelter, while these people disobey their Creator and fail to recognize his beneficence or Satan's harm.
[ALUSI-FULL:v19p25/r2] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · author | holds | Animals pursue benefit and avoid harm, while these people neither seek the great reward nor avoid punishment and fail to follow the true path.
[ALUSI-FULL:v19p25/r3] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · author | holds | If animals lack true belief that leads to good, they also do not adopt falsehood that produces evil; people instead build false premises and derive harmful rules from them.
[ALUSI-FULL:v19p25/r4] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · author | holds | Animal error affects only themselves, but human ignorance causes strife, corruption, obstruction of right guidance, and disorder among people.
[ALUSI-FULL:v19p25/r5] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · author | holds | Animals use their innate faculties for their proper purposes, whereas these people disable reason and neglect the original human disposition.
[ALUSI-FULL:v19p25/r6] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · الصوفية وجماعة من الناس | reports | Some infer from the comparison that animals do not know their Lord; Sufis and others instead hold that animals know and glorify God, treating the comparison as outward language.
[ALUSI-FULL:v19p25/r7] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · قيل | reports | An alternative says the comparison concerns failure to benefit from Qur'anic verses and cosmic or personal signs; animal knowledge of God is innate rather than inferential.
[ALUSI-FULL:v19p25/r8] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · قيل | reports | On that view, people are more astray because animals were granted knowledge of God and glorify him through it, while these people were not granted it.
[ELMALILI:25:43-44/r10] ELMALILI, d. 1361 · author | holds | Cattle use their given faculties as intended and lack beliefs in both good and evil, whereas these people fail even to recognize their Lord and repay His favors with ingratitude.
[ELMALILI:25:43-44/r11] ELMALILI, d. 1361 · author | holds | They

[ELMALILI:25:43-44/r7] ELMALILI, d. 1361 · author | holds | Most neither heed transmitted evidence nor act through rational evidence.
[ELMALILI:25:43-44/r8] ELMALILI, d. 1361 · author | holds | They resemble cattle because they do not use reason or hearing and follow only their sensations.

[IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p37/r1] IBNASHUR-FULL, d. 1393 · author | holds | The passage moves from despair over their desire-dominated minds to warning against assuming they grasp proofs; the disjunctive am shifts from one denial to another and coordinates an implied question. | mentions 25:42
[IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p37/r2] IBNASHUR-FULL, d. 1393 · author | holds | Denying that most hear means they do not understand the truth in the message; one who doubts it is like someone who never heard it, as in the cited analogy. | mentions 27:80
[IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p37/r3] IBNASHUR-FULL, d. 1393 · author | holds | The alternative of reason concerns nonverbal signs in created things, which they also fail to understand. | mentions 10:101
[IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p37/r4] IBNASHUR-FULL, d. 1393 · author | holds | The verse says most rather than all because ordinary followers lack insight, while some intelligent people read cosmic signs but pride and status keep them from following the Prophet alongside poor and enslaved believers such as ʿAmmār and Bilāl.
[IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p37/r5] IBNASHUR-FULL, d. 1393 · author | holds | The cattle comparison explains how sound senses can receive the call yet yield no benefit when people are not disposed to attend; it approximates their lack of understanding.
[IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p37/r6] IBNASHUR-FULL, d. 1393 · author | holds | Abū al-Ṭayyib's verse illustrates that someone may surpass people while still belonging to their kind; the plural pronouns refer to the majority according to the noun's meaning.
[TABATABAI:25:43-44/r4] TABATABAI, d. 1402 · author | holds | Am is disjunctive, hisab means supposition, and the plural pronouns refer semantically to the relative clause in the previous verse.
[TABATABAI:25:43-44/r5] TABATABAI, d. 1402 · author | holds | People reach life's felicity either by reasoning to recognize and follow truth or, if unable to reason independently, by hearing and following someone who knows and advises them. | mentions 67:10
[TABATABAI:25:44-46/r1] TABATABAI, d. 1402 · author | holds | The question asks whether most can hear truth or reason it out and follow it; the answer explains that they do neither, like livestock that cannot grasp meaning beyond sounds.
[TABATABAI:25:44-46/r2] TABATABAI, d. 1402 · author | holds | They are more astray than livestock because animals avoid what harms them, while these people prefer harm to benefit; animals also lack the human equipment for guidance that people possess.
[TABATABAI:25:44-46/r3] TABATABAI, d. 1402 · بعضهم | reports | Some infer from the comparison that livestock have no knowledge of their Lord.
[TABATABAI:25:44-46/r4] TABATABAI, d. 1402 · author | rejects | Tabatabai says the verse denies neither basic knowledge of God in livestock nor in disbelievers; it denies disbelievers' following innate rational truth, which desire has veiled, and compares them with livestock lacking that kind of perception.
[TABATABAI:25:44-46/r5] TABATABAI, d. 1402 · بعضهم | reports | Another answer says the wording speaks only according to outward appearance; Tabatabai says that claim cannot be established by argument.
[ASAD-NOTES:25:43#n37/r1] ASAD-NOTES, d. 1412 · author | holds | Asad glosses “even less conscious of the right way” as being farther astray from the path of truth, linking 7:179. | mentions 7:179
[ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p356/r2] ISLAHI-TADABBUR · author | holds | Verses 35-44 invoke earlier messengers and rejecters to encourage patience; rejecters are worse than animals and enslaved to desire, while the Prophet must convey truth rather than force acceptance.
[ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p375/r4] ISLAHI-TADABBUR · author | holds | The Moses and Noah narratives and intervening peoples assure the Prophet and warn his nation: earlier communities mocked messengers who taught them and ultimately suffered a terrible fate; the next sūrah gives these events in detail.
[ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p380/r4] ISLAHI-TADABBUR · author | holds | These verses reassure the Prophet: intellect guides, while desire enslaves, and those who abandon intellect cannot be guided.
[ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p380/r7] ISLAHI-TADABBUR · author | holds | The question addresses the Prophet, who was exerting himself to reform people, and asks whether he expects them still to understand.
[ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p380/r8] ISLAHI-TADABBUR · author | holds | They have squandered their capacity to understand and become like animals, indeed worse.
[ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p380/r9] ISLAHI-TADABBUR · author | holds | The comparison is precise rather than hyperbolic: animals follow the instincts God created in them without deviation.
[ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p381/r1] ISLAHI-TADABBUR · author | holds | A person enslaved to desire exceeds natural limits and becomes worse than an animal.
[KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:25:43/r2] KURANYOLU-TEFSIR · author | holds | The Qur'an opposes the mindset that deifies base desires; while people persist in it, they cannot understand the Prophet's call or reason soundly and are more astray than animals.
[KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:25:43/r3] KURANYOLU-TEFSIR · author | holds | These verses criticize Meccan polytheists while teaching a universal lesson: across history, people wrongly rank bodily desires, material interests, and status above reason, sound belief, and justice.
[QIRAAT-ER:25:44:2#1/r1] QIRAAT-ER · author | holds | Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī read taḥsibu while the other readers use taḥsabu; this Najdī–Ḥijāzī vowel difference leaves the meaning unchanged.
[STUDYQURAN:25:44/r1] STUDYQURAN · author | holds | Disbelievers resemble cattle because they do not think and limit their concerns to eating and drinking; unlike humans, cattle are not condemned for this.
[STUDYQURAN:25:44/r2] STUDYQURAN · some commentators | reports | Cattle follow their natures, obey herders, and can hear and understand as animals, while disbelievers disobey God and lack ears and eyes for truth.
[STUDYQURAN:25:44/r3] STUDYQURAN · some commentators | reports | Cattle lack knowledge but do not have the compound ignorance of neither knowing nor knowing that they do not know.
[STUDYQURAN:25:44/r4] STUDYQURAN · some commentators | reports | Cattle know what benefits or harms them, whereas some people fail to recognize God’s goodness and Satan as enemy, and so cannot seek the Hereafter’s good and avoid punishment.
